rubric_hint.rule: 12 eligible species recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, none within 250 m
rubric_hint.basis: prompts/rubric.md v1 applied to all rings 0-1000 m and effort; a default, not a verdict

reasons.claim: Notified regeneration felling, 0.6 ha polygon in Lekeberg. Completed felling from 2006 overlaps 9.2% (0.055 ha), so not already felled.

No records inside the polygon or within 250 m, and no near-site recording days. Effort across 1000 m is far above the county median (5871 records vs 128.5; 100th percentile), so the near-site gap is not explained by low recording around the site.

The rubric hint reports 12 eligible species beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, giving MEDIUM. Within 500 m, 5 eligible site-bound species were recorded. The nearest is the VU lichen Gyalecta truncigena at 253 m (2018, 5 m uncertainty). Others: VU Megalaria grossa at 335 m, VU Gyalecta flotowii at 421 m, CR lichen Catapyrenium psoromoides at 436 m (4 records, latest 2025), and VU fungus Hypoxylon vogesiacum at 449 m (2024). Their listed threats include lack of continuity forest and of old/large trees.

uncertainties: The nearest eligible record is 253 m away, just outside the 250 m ring, and dates from 2018. It may not reflect the small 0.6 ha stand.
I looked in detail only at the 500 m ring. The other 7 eligible species the hint counts lie between 500 and 1000 m and I did not inspect them.
The polygon is small (equivalent radius 44 m), so nearby records say little about its interior.
not_established: Whether any threatened species occurs inside the polygon.
That the site is safe to fell.
Absence of records within 250 m does not show absence of species.
next_action: Reviewer should check where the 253-449 m lichen and fungus records lie relative to the polygon and whether the stand has similar old-forest features. A field check is advisable because no records exist within 250 m.
